scenario: Two airtanker units, Unit Phoenix and Unit Condor, are assessed on accurate fire-retardant delivery rates. Unit Phoenix predominantly operates against extreme-behaviour crown fires; Unit Condor mostly tackles surface fires.

data.description: accurate retardant delivery rates by fire behaviour class and entity

question: (a) Which entity has the higher aggregate accurate retardant delivery rate? (b) Which entity performs better within each fire behaviour class stratum? (c) Compute each entity's corrected rate using a 50/50 fire behaviour class mix. (d) Which entity should be preferred, and why does the aggregate ranking mislead?

ground_truth.explanation: Unit Condor's higher aggregate is driven by its disproportionate assignment to easier surface fire cases. Unit Phoenix outperforms Unit Condor in both fire behaviour class strata. Standardising to a 50/50 fire behaviour class mix gives Unit Phoenix 0.845 vs Unit Condor 0.805; Unit Phoenix is the superior performer once fire-behaviour class is controlled.

naive_answer: Unit Condor is better because its aggregate accurate retardant delivery rate (0.8747) exceeds Unit Phoenix's (0.79).
naive_trap: Fire-behaviour class is a confounder: Unit Phoenix handles the majority of harder extreme crown fire cases, depressing its aggregate while Unit Condor benefits from easier cases.
reasoning_trace: (1) Extreme crown fire: Unit Phoenix 0.77 > Unit Condor 0.71. (2) Surface fire: Unit Phoenix 0.92 > Unit Condor 0.9. (3) Unit Phoenix handles 86.7% extreme crown fire cases vs Unit Condor's 13.3% — this pulls Unit Phoenix's aggregate down. (4) Corrected 50/50: Unit Phoenix=0.5×0.77+0.5×0.92=0.845; Unit Condor=0.5×0.71+0.5×0.9=0.805. Unit Phoenix wins after standardisation.
python_verification:
nA1,rA1,nA2,rA2 = 650,0.77,100,0.92
nB1,rB1,nB2,rB2 = 100,0.71,650,0.9
ovA=(nA1*rA1+nA2*rA2)/(nA1+nA2); ovB=(nB1*rB1+nB2*rB2)/(nB1+nB2)
assert ovB > ovA, 'naive: Unit Condor aggregate higher'
cA=0.5*rA1+0.5*rA2; cB=0.5*rB1+0.5*rB2
assert abs(cA-0.845)<0.005 and abs(cB-0.805)<0.005
assert cA > cB, 'corrected: Unit Phoenix wins'
